name: Lydia
charge: A seller of purple who worshipped God; whose heart the Lord opened; who constrained the apostles to abide in her house
summary: At Philippi there was no synagogue, so on the sabbath day Paul and his companions went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was accustomed to be made, and sat down and spoke to the women who resorted there. A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard them, and the Lord opened her heart so that she attended to the things spoken by Paul. She and her household were baptized, and she constrained the apostles to come into her house and abide there.
offenseFull: From Troas they came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis, and from there to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia and a colony (Acts 16:11-12). There were but few Israelites resident at Philippi, since no mention is made of any synagogue in it; there was instead a place outside the city by the river side where the people were known to gather for prayer, and that is where Paul and his companions resorted on the sabbath day and sat down and spoke to the women which resorted there (Acts 16:13). There were still our people in Philippi, which is who the letter to the Philippians is written to, addressed to all the saints in Christ Jesus which are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons (Philippians 1:1).

Among these was Lydia, a seller of purple of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, who had taken up her residence at Philippi for the sake of her trade (Acts 16:14). She moved for her work, the same as people today move to another city because the work there pays better. And the Lord opened her heart so that she attended to the things which were spoken of Paul: the Lord gave the increase, he put his spirit on this sister, and she was not worried about the day-to-day. When she was baptized, and her household, she besought them, saying that if they had judged her to be faithful to the Lord they should come into her house and abide there, and she constrained them (Acts 16:15). She urged them, because she recognized a prophet when she heard one. She already had the lodging and the hospitality set up for the prophets, and with that family the apostle and his companions took up their abode during their stay at Philippi, which is said to have been many days. That is the spirit our foremothers rolled in, and it is the spirit of Christ.
judgmentFull: Her house did not close when the trouble came. After the magistrates had beaten Paul and Silas and afterward brought them out of the prison, they went out of the prison and entered into the house of Lydia, and when they had seen the brethren they comforted them and departed (Acts 16:40). The men who had been stripped and beaten in that city in the morning had her doors opened to them again the same day. The lodging she had asked for became the gathering place of the congregation in that city after the public hostility.

Paul afterward wrote back to that city thanking them for their fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now (Philippians 1:3-5), and reminding them that in the beginning of the gospel, when he departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with him concerning giving and receiving but they only, for even in Thessalonica they sent once and again to his necessity (Philippians 4:15-16). Philippi was the congregation that carried the labourers, and the first door opened in it was hers.

text.text: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis;
And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.
And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted thither.
Paul and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus which are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons:
And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.
And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us.
And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
I thank my God upon every remembrance of you,
Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy,
For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now;
Now ye Philippians know also, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with me as concerning giving and receiving, but ye only.
For even in Thessalonica ye sent once and again unto my necessity.
Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality.
